vector_search_best_practices.overview: Best practices for setting up and optimizing vector search systems using Milvus and local Hugging Face (sentence-transformers) embeddings.

principle.name: Generate Embeddings Efficiently
principle.description: Embed with the local sentence-transformers model loaded by load_embedding_model()

best_practices.practice: Encode documents in batches rather than one at a time
Load the model once and reuse it
Normalize embeddings to match the COSINE metric
Use the same model for documents and queries

principle.name: Embedding Dimension Consistency
principle.description: Ensure dimensions match across all components

validation_checklist.item: Test with sample data before bulk ingestion

principle.name: Tune the IVF_FLAT Index
principle.description: The index and search settings are in schema.py (INDEX_PARAMS and SEARCH_PARAMS)

parameter.name: nlist
parameter.description: Number of clusters the vectors are divided into when the index is built

tuning.guideline: A new value takes effect when the index is rebuilt

parameter.name: nprobe
parameter.description: Number of clusters searched per query (up to nlist)

tuning.guideline: Start with the value in SEARCH_PARAMS, increase if recall is insufficient

principle.name: Choose Appropriate Distance Metric
principle.description: Select distance metric based on embedding characteristics

metric.name: COSINE
metric.use_case: Most common, works with normalized embeddings

principle.name: Implement Robust Ingestion Pipeline
principle.description: Build reliable data ingestion with error handling

best_practices.practice: Check the connection and the schema before inserting
Insert one row per product with the fields in schema.py, then flush
Build the index and load the collection after the insert, as insert_sample_data.py does

principle.name: Filter on Scalar Fields
principle.description: Narrow the search with a filter expression on the fields in schema.py
principle.example:
from schema import PRODUCT_OUTPUT_FIELDS, SEARCH_PARAMS, VECTOR_FIELD
def search_with_filters( query: str, filters: dict, top_k: int = 10 ): """Search with filters on the product fields"""
query_vector = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)[0].tolist()
# Build filter expression for Milvus filter_conditions = [] for key, value in filters.items(): if isinstance(value, str): filter_conditions.append(f'{key} == "{value}"') elif isinstance(value, list): values_str = ', '.join([f'"{v}"' for v in value]) filter_conditions.append(f'{key} in [{values_str}]') else: filter_conditions.append(f'{key} == {value}')
filter_expr = " AND ".join(filter_conditions)
results = client.search( collection_name=collection_name, data=[query_vector], anns_field=VECTOR_FIELD, search_params=SEARCH_PARAMS, limit=top_k, filter=filter_expr, output_fields=PRODUCT_OUTPUT_FIELDS )
return results
# Example usage (the category values are in sample_products_en.py and sample_products_ja.py) results = search_with_filters( query="lightweight laptop", filters={"category": ["Computer", "Camera"]}, top_k=5 )

pitfall.mistake: Not testing connection before bulk ingestion
pitfall.consequence: Wasted time and resources on failed ingestion
pitfall.solution: Always validate connection and schema before ingestion
Always batch embed and insert operations
Filter on the scalar fields in schema.py

principle.name: Secure Credentials Management

best_practices.practice: Use environment variables for all credentials
Use .env files for local development (add to .gitignore)
Use secrets management services in production
Use SSL/TLS when the server supports it (the instructor's Milvus for this hands-on does not, so connect over http://)

principle.example:
# .env.example file MILVUS_HOST=your-milvus-host.com MILVUS_PORT=19530 MILVUS_USER=your-username MILVUS_PASSWORD=your-password EMBEDDING_MODEL=paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 COLLECTION_NAME=products_your_name
# Load in code from dotenv import load_dotenv import os
load_dotenv()
# Use environment variables milvus_host = os.getenv("MILVUS_HOST") embedding_model = os.getenv("EMBEDDING_MODEL")
